narr: Deep monsoon moisture over Arizona and an approaching trough of low pressure from the Pacific Northwest helped produce local flash flooding and large hail. Thunderstorms reformed during the evening over Yavapai County which continued flash flooding in smaller streams and rapid rises on The Verde River (a main stem river).
ev: The Paria River gauge at Lees Ferry showed a 4 foot rise between 6:00 AM and 7:00 AM MST. The Paria River drainage originates in Utah and flows into the Colorado River near Lees Ferry.
The East Verde River near Childs (EVDA3) had a 2.9 foot rise between 0800 and 0845 MST.
The Tonto Creek stream gauge above Gun Creek (TNRA3) measured a 3.1 foot rise between 0845 and 1000 AM MST.
The water was flowing 4.85 feet deep (normally dry) in Munds Canyon under Interstate 17 and about 25 feet wide. The estimated flow was 900 CFS.
Granite Creek in Prescott (GCRA3) rose from 7.17 to 10.22 feet in 45 minutes.

Pictures on social media show at least 10 inches of water flowing in Dinnebito Wash near Hardrock. The water had been flowing for at least 2 hours. Road going into Hardrock were not passible due to the water flowing over the roadways.
Granite Creek (GRWA3) below Watson Lake rose 2.2 feet to 3.97 feet in one hour and 44 minutes. Water crested at 7:20 PM MST.
The Wet Beaver Creek gauge (BCMA3) near Montezuma Castle National Monument rose from 1.0 to 3.03 feet in 65 minutes. It crested at 11:13 PM MST.
The Verde River near Clarkdale rose over 17 feet in 58 minutes (VDCA3). The water crested at 19.49 feet at 942 PM MST.
The Verde River near Camp Verde rose just over 10 feet in 4 hours (VAVA3). The water crested at 14.23 at 9:30 AM MST.
Emergency Management reported a 4 foot rise on Black Canyon Creek at 8:08 PM MST. This creek is downsteam from parts of the Tiger Fire (2021).
